expectation: This should help make a cell boundary that oxygen can cross.

effect: The fats first needed water to form a membrane patch; the result says oxygen can cross its oily middle and channels speed up water crossing.
reaction: I was surprised that water, rather than oxygen, was needed to form the patch.

reaction: It is satisfying to see the pore fitted into the boundary.
reason: The sugar-carrier picture shows a protein spanning the membrane with a pocket for sugar, matching the remaining carrier goal.

reaction: The separate routes make the two proteins' jobs easier to picture.
reason: The oxygen goal remains, and the picture showed oxygen crossing the membrane's oily middle.

choice.combine: Membrane with water and sugar routes

expectation: Oxygen should cross the membrane and complete the remaining goal.

effect: Oxygen crossed the lipid patch, completing the last goal; the picture shows more moving into the cell than out.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the boundary work without breaking the cell outline.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the water channel was most worthwhile because the picture made its job clear: a pore through the boundary lets water pass both ways.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final oxygen combination felt a little repetitive because the membrane patch result had already said oxygen crosses its oily middle.

surprise.text: I expected oxygen to combine with the fats first, but the game instead paired the fats with water to make the membrane patch.

arbitrary.text: The need to combine fats with water first was not obvious to me from the starting pictures, although the resulting picture showed where the water-facing heads go.

continue.text: I would probably try another chapter: seeing the separate water and sugar routes made cell parts easier to picture, though I hope later choices offer more to figure out.
